paper.title: Making the Cut: A Bandit-based Approach to Tiered Interviewing

settings.name_in_paper: Tiered interviewing, PAC combinatorial pure exploration (CACO setting)
unmapped: Multi-stage (tiered) process with m stages; at stage i a pull costs j_i and has information gain s_i (reward is sigma/sqrt(s_i)-sub-Gaussian); only K_i arms survive stage i
Goal: identify a K-subset with linear objective w within epsilon of optimum, using individual base-arm pulls
settings.definition_quote: For each stage $i\in [m]$ the user defines a cost $j_i$ and an information gain $s_i$ for the type of pull (type of interview) being used in that stage. During each stage, $K_i$ arms move on to the next stage

settings.name_in_paper: Tiered interviewing, fixed-budget combinatorial pure exploration (BRUTaS setting)
unmapped: Multi-stage process with per-stage budgets Tbar_i, per-pull cost j_i and information gain s_i, and Ktilde_i accept/reject decisions per stage
Goal: identify the exact optimal K-subset under a linear objective w (combinatorial pure exploration)
settings.definition_quote: Algorithm~\ref{alg:bug_cut} provides pseudocode for \brutas, which takes as input fixed budgets $\bar{T}_i$ for each stage $i \in [m]$, where $\sum_{i\in[m]}\bar{T}_i=\bar{T}$, the total budget. ... let $\tilde{K}_i$ represent how many decisions we need to make at stage $i\in[m]$

algorithms.name: CACO (Cutting Arms using a Combinatorial Oracle)

symbols.j_i: cost of a pull at stage i
symbols.s_i: information gain of a pull at stage i
symbols.K_i: number of arms kept after stage i
symbols.X_i: sum over active arms a in A_{i-1} of min{1/Delta_a^2, K_i^2/epsilon^2}
symbols.Delta_a: combinatorial gap score of arm a (Chen et al. 2014)

conditions: each arm reward has mean u(a) with sigma-sub-Gaussian tail (sigma/sqrt(s_i) for stage-i pulls)

source.label: thm:scuc
source.quote: Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the \cut\ algorithm (Algorithm~\ref{alg:conf_cut}) returns the set $\out$ where $w(\out)-w(M_m^*) < \epsilon$ and T \leq O(\sigma^2\sum_{i\in[m]}( \frac{j_i}{s_i}(\sum_{a\in A_{i-1}} \min\{\frac{1}{\Delta_a^2},\frac{K_i^2}{\epsilon^2}\})\log(\frac{\sigma^2j_i^4}{s_i\delta}\sum_{a\in A_{i-1}} \min\{\frac{1}{\Delta_a^2},\frac{K_i^2}{\epsilon^2}\}))).

results.notes: T is the total cost (weighted by j_i), not the number of pulls. Restated as Theorem 3 in the appendix, where the proof gives explicit constant 499 and min{4/Delta_a^2, K_i^2/eps^2}. The returned set is epsilon-optimal w.p. >= 1-delta. Reduces to CLUCB bound for one stage.

symbols.s_b: information gain of a pull at stage b
symbols.j_b: cost of a pull at stage b
symbols.Ktilde_b: number of accept/reject decisions at stage b
symbols.H_tilde: max_i i*Delta_(i)^{-2} with sorted combinatorial gaps

conditions: total budget sum_i Tbar_i > K (number of arms n)
each arm reward has mean u(a) with sigma-sub-Gaussian tail

source.label: thm:bcut
source.quote: Then, Algorithm~\ref{alg:bug_cut} uses at most $\bar{T}_i$ samples per stage $i\in[m]$ and outputs a solution $\out\in\mathcal{M}_K\cup\{\perp\}$ such that \Pr[\out\neq M_*] \leq  n^2\exp\left(-\frac{\sum_{b=1}^m s_b(\bar{T}_b-\tilde{K}_b)/(j_b\tlog(\tilde{K}_b))}{72\sigma^2\tilde{\mathbf{H}}}\right)

results.notes: Paper's n (number of arms) mapped to K. Restated as Theorem 4 in the appendix. Reduces to CSAR bound for one stage.
